scope: Source-runtime diagnostic; not packaged or release certification

result.text:
I inspected the FieldOps work-order web app, focusing on the `src/storage.js` and `src/work-orders.js` modules, along with their corresponding test files (`tests/storage.test.js` and `tests/work-orders.test.js`). The baseline test suite failed with two distinct defects: the status filter logic in `filterWorkOrders` was not correctly combining status and search queries, and the `loadWorkOrders` function in `src/storage.js` crashed when parsing invalid JSON strings instead of gracefully falling back to default data.

To repair the status filter defect, I modified `src/work-orders.js` to ensure the `filterWorkOrders` function applies both the status and search filters simultaneously. The fix introduced a `matchesStatus` check that validates the status field against the provided filter, while the search logic remains case-insensitive across IDs, titles, and sites. This ensures that when both filters are active, a work order is only returned if it matches the status AND contains the search query string.

To repair the invalid saved browser data defect, I updated `src/storage.js` to wrap the `JSON.parse` call in a `try-catch` block. If parsing fails (e.g., due to malformed JSON), the function now catches the error and returns the provided fallback data instead of crashing. Additionally, I added a validation step to check if the saved data has the correct shape (an array of objects with required properties) before attempting to parse it, ensuring robust handling of unexpected input formats.

The existing test suite now passes completely, confirming that the status filter works correctly with search and that the app handles invalid saved browser data gracefully without stopping the application. The current design and public behavior have been preserved, and no external dependencies were added.
